note: A DISPATCH SCRIPT RUNS FROM WHEREVER THE DISPATCHER IS STANDING, AND NOBODY RECORDS WHERE THAT WAS. Reported by the Lefford queue operator 2026-08-29 while launching the-overture, unprompted, and worth having beyond the one merge it affected. The queue drain executes scripts/sluice-run.sh from the OPERATOR CHECKOUT, whatever branch that is on -- not from main, and not from the candidate. merge_phases is read from the script own location before it cd-s into the worktree. Decision 0426 restored heavy to the merge phase list; the operator checkout was still on a personal fix branch predating 0426 carrying the four-phase list, so THE FIRST MERGE AFTER 0426 LANDED (the-errata) WAS GATED WITH THE OLD PHASES. Nothing objected. Its content was a comment-only cost correction so nothing escaped that heavy could have observed, and the operator caught it before launching the next merge and disclosed it rather than quietly fixing the checkout. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE ALREADY-KNOWN heavy-remote SHAPE: heavy-remote runs main copy of heavy-run.sh, which is at least a known shared gated state you can look up. An operator working branch is not observable from the queue at all. A queue row records PHASE TIMINGS but nothing compares the phases that RAN against the phases that SHOULD have run, so a short-list gating is byte-indistinguishable from a full one in every artifact a reader consults. THREE CONSEQUENCES WORTH CARRYING. (1) A campaign that changes a phase list does not run its own new list -- the NEXT merge does, so do not read your own green as coverage of your change. (2) A campaign that changes heavy-run.sh, census-run.sh or sluice-run.sh cannot verify the change by dispatching; say so in the record and name the first run that will exercise it. The Governor already paid this one, dispatching a real run to verify a fix that correctly did not fire. (3) The cheap guard nobody has written: have the drain log which phase list it resolved, next to the row, so the artifact a reader consults carries the thing that varied. Offered as a suggestion, not a claim that it is the right fix -- sluice-run.sh dispatch path is campaign-grade risk and off the board lane by convention.
